limitations: This is a reviewed derivative benchmark, not upstream official tests.
Existing scenario assertions and shared helpers were strengthened, without changing scenario identities, denominator, seeds, requirements or app implementations.
Presence text permits duplicates; named action/object identities remain strict.
Known missing business branches, exact fare serialization remain unresolved; this review does not claim zero false negatives or complete prose coverage.
Fixed clock synchronization, 60-second scenario runtime and real persistence/permissions require end-to-end testing; no full app was run by this reviewer.
This is a derivative benchmark source review, not an upstream official-score certification.
BOOK-09 broader prose coverage and BOOK-11 parent-entry/text-scope/tag-serialization ambiguities remain explicit.
Extension scenarios were executed against a manually extended reference fixture, not a ShallowCode-generated candidate; this validates oracle feasibility, not an official full-application pass rate.
Existing 24/35 identities were preserved; the revision now has 26 atomic requirements and 49 scenarios, so older scores are not directly comparable.
Draft-title activity leakage and page/chapter deletion are newly covered; full eight-task and multi-candidate behavior is outside this review.
No generated Ctrip application was read or reevaluated; no claims of measured business pass rate or zero false negatives.
Explicit pre-existing public accessibility/record naming contracts remain; these are derivative benchmark conventions, not proof of upstream product necessity.

Visual similarity and unspecified multi-city/fulfillment/phone-email-completion/context behaviors remain outside concrete scenario coverage.
All 100 callbacks reviewed, but review is not 100 complete application executions.
Generic token/diff oracles and incomplete rejection/atomicity/permission cases remain open.
No screenshot equivalence claim; references used for context, not a hidden DOM schema.

No extra ARIA metadata group introduced. Existing public Branch state and membership groups are preserved. Assignee option selected state, distinct team-submit name and clone-value label/state are explicitly part of the new public observation contract.
The original external benchmark, all generated applications and prior scores remain unchanged.
Source review and targeted contract probes do not establish measured real-application false-negative rates or all 33 business passes.
Existing explicit role/name contracts remain derivative benchmark conventions. No new ARIA structure or source semantics introduced.
Broader keyboard, icon, highlight visual emphasis, Undo reload and second-setting behavior are not fully tested.
Multiline DOM text, clipped accessible labels and auxiliary regions in an empty collection retain explicitly documented representation risks.
The existing broad light-green pixel threshold is a bounded visual oracle; it is not screenshot similarity or proof that every human-recognized light-green shade is accepted.
Derivative benchmark review only; untouched upstream official tests and scores are not changed by this review.
Two disclosed ROOT clarifications affect historical comparability. Denominator remains 55 requirements/86 scenarios.
No complete generated application was evaluated. Synthetic helper contracts do not prove business completion or benchmark score improvement.
Reference-image pixels/layout were not audited. Source/name/caption transitions do not fully prove visual content or enlarged-image content. Distinct high-resolution image URLs are legitimate.
Anonymous hidden wishlist persistence is not observable through the scoped permission prompt; no adding-membership workflow or private API is invented.
Remember-me lifetime, actual mailbox delivery and guest completion remain unspecified.
Invoice oracle checks filename/reference and PDF header, not full PDF document parsing/content.
An automatic carousel transition may coincide with Next activation.
Monetary associations are bounded to disclosed public forms with selected-record identity and strict visible ambiguity; arbitrary global numbers/first matches are not accepted.
Static semantic review and synthetic contract tests are not execution of a complete spreadsheet application and do not establish a quantitative false-negative rate.
The fixed 100 scenarios do not exercise every conditional infrastructure failure without a public reproducible trigger, arbitrary larger datasets or every combination of operations.
The visible grid/sample dataset is observed; unrendered offscreen cells cannot be directly inspected by the public-DOM oracle.
Existing explicit ARIA roles/names are retained benchmark contracts; screenshot similarity and excluded collaboration/authentication features are not scored.
CSV serialization/numeric presentation were clarified and one existing CSV fixture now covers already-required UTF-8 Chinese; old outcomes are not transferred to this version.
This is a model-assisted review of a derivative benchmark, not upstream official certification or human annotation.
No generated applications or scores were consulted; no application/controller/source-requirement data was modified.
The 66-scenario denominator is preserved. Expired-comment boundaries and identified broader editor/rendering/history behaviors remain unmeasured.
Public UI privacy/ownership checks do not certify private endpoint authorization or internal database retention.
Date/time parsers cover stated UTC and ordinary English presentations; this does not establish zero false negatives across all international display formats.
Role/name conventions explicitly stated in the benchmark remain scoring contracts; passing them is not a complete real-world quality metric.
